cards.name: Rolling Shutter Repair
cards.summary: Analyses moving CMOS footage and removes rolling-shutter skew and wobble (leaning verticals, jello) caused by fast pans or vibration. Corrective only: on a static or still frame there is no visible change.
use_for: fix leaning buildings / poles in fast phone or DSLR pans of rally crowds
remove jello from drone or vehicle-mounted news footage
clean whip pans before speed-ramping them in a trailer
repair handheld B-roll before Warp Stabilizer
avoid: expecting any change on still photos or locked-off shots
using it on footage without rolling shutter (adds warping artefacts)
stacking with Warp Stabilizer's own Enhanced Reduction on the same clip (double correction)

params.name: Rolling Shutter Rate
params.does: Percentage of the frame time spent scanning; how strongly skew is corrected
params.typical: 50 (default); Adobe guidance: DSLRs roughly 50-70, phones closer to 100. Raise if verticals still lean, lower if it over-corrects

params.name: Scan Direction
params.typical: 1 (Top -> Bottom) for normal landscape footage; try 3/4 for footage shot with the camera/phone rotated 90 degrees (e.g. vertical phone video), check visually

params.name: Method
params.typical: 1 (Warp) normally; 2 (Pixel Motion) for complex motion, slower

params.name: Detailed Analysis
params.does: More thorough analysis pass for the Warp method

params.name: Pixel Motion Detail
params.does: Detail of the optical-flow field when Method = Pixel Motion

cards.scripting: Needs real camera motion; demo_settings will look unchanged on a still photo or a locked-off clip (that is expected, not a failure). Pixel Motion Detail only matters when Method = 2. Apply before stabilising, scaling or speed changes. Verified 2026-10-04: an aerender of a freshly applied instance on the locked-off test plate A showed no 'Analyzing' banner (unlike Warp Stabilizer) and differed from an untouched render only by a warp of at most 1 px (mean 1.5/255), so the effect runs at render time but had no skew to fix; a visible demo needs real rolling-shutter pan footage. Whether it also runs a background analysis worth waiting for is unverified (low confidence): check the output before relying on it. Measured on a 300 px/s pan with a synthetic 48 px skew (live wave 3): the correction is about Rolling Shutter Rate % of one frame of pan motion (Rate 80: 9.5 px of 1920, Rate 100: 10-12 px), which is all a real sensor can skew (readout time <= one frame); the test plate's extra skew stayed, as it should.

verified.note: On the skewed pan the vertical bars stand visibly straighter than in the control frame (bottom-to-top skew down from 37 to 28 px of 1920 on average), i.e. it removes rolling-shutter skew, by the share Rolling Shutter Rate 80 allows.

previous.why: the test footage has nothing for it to act on (see note), so the render could not show it doing its job
judged on the live wave 3 re-render on the second (synthetic) footage set, which has what the card acts on
previous.note: Frame equals an untouched render of the clip at the same instant except for a warp of at most 1 px (mean 1.5/255 vs no-op gallery renders, which are bit-identical to each other; no banner): the effect ran, but the locked-off clip has no rolling-shutter skew (its frame-to-frame jumps are exposure flashes, not motion), so no demo value can make it visible; status is now needs_input (needs skewed phone/DSLR pan footage).
previous.second_opinion: corrected: agree with needs_input, but the frame is not identical/encode noise: it differs from bit-identical no-op renders by a real <=1 px warp with no banner, so the note and scripting now say the effect ran with nothing to fix, and the unverified 'render only after background analysis finishes' claim was softened

cards.name: Smear
cards.summary: Moves the image area inside a source mask to a new position and smears the surrounding pixels within a boundary mask, like pushing wet paint. Shows nothing until two masks exist on the layer.
use_for: comic stretch of an object or a clearly-labelled satire caricature
pull a logo or element out of place for a gooey transition
subtle reshaping of a region (prefer Puppet / Liquify today)
avoid: distorting a real politician's or reporter's face in news/explainer content (reads as manipulated media)
legacy effect: Liquify, Puppet Tool or Mesh Warp usually look cleaner
large Mask Offset values tear and stretch pixels visibly
masks that are open or overlap the layer edge

params.name: Source Mask
params.typical: a small closed mask around the feature to push

params.name: Boundary Mask
params.does: Mask limiting the area that may distort
params.typical: a larger closed mask enclosing the source mask

params.name: Mask Offset
params.does: Where the source mask content is moved to (layer pixels)
params.typical: 2D point in layer pixels (default [1056, 540]); move it 20-120 px from the default to push the source area that far

params.name: Percent
params.does: How much of the smear is applied

params.name: Elasticity
params.does: Popup: how stiff or fluid the surrounding image behaves
params.typical: 1 Stiff (default); 4 Normal; 7-9 Loose / Liquid / Super Fluid

params.name: Interpolation Method
params.does: How the smear is interpolated over time

cards.scripting: Source Mask and Boundary Mask are mask references (indices of masks on the same layer) and cannot be set from a spec; create two closed masks first, then pick them in the effect. Mask Offset is in layer pixel space. Percent defaults to 0, so nothing moves until Percent is raised. Interpolation Method: 1 Discrete, 2 Linear (default), 3 Smooth; Elasticity: 1 Stiff ... 9 Super Fluid (enum_labels, read from After Effects 26.0).

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (needs two masks on the layer), so no gallery frame was rendered.

cards.name: Spherize
cards.summary: Wraps a circular area of the layer around a sphere so the centre bulges toward the viewer, like a fisheye or magnifying glass. Bulge only; it cannot pinch.
use_for: comic big-head / bulging face punch in satire reels
magnifier highlight on a document or headline
bulge-pop transition on a beat
fisheye skate-video style on reel B-roll
avoid: leaving it on a serious news face (looks mocking)
radius much larger than half the frame: the whole picture warps and the bulge stops reading as a highlight
using it for pinch (min radius 0; use Bulge with negative height)

params.name: Radius
params.does: Radius of the sphere in pixels; 0 = off

params.name: Center of Sphere
params.typical: on the face or object to emphasise, e.g. [960, 540]

cards.scripting: Center of Sphere is in layer pixels (same as comp pixels for a full-frame 1920x1080 layer). Radius 0 disables it, so it is safe to keyframe from 0.

verified.note: Clear magnifier bulge centred on the middle of the frame: the stripes curve outward and the figures bow around the centre while the frame edges stay put.

cards.name: Transform
cards.summary: Applies position, scale, skew, rotation and opacity inside the effect stack, with its own shutter angle so animated moves get motion blur without the layer motion-blur switch. The workhorse for punch-ins, shakes and whip moves.
use_for: motion-blurred punch-in zoom on a quote or reaction beat
whip-pan / slide transitions with built-in blur
beat-synced scale bumps in reels
re-frame or tilt a shot after other effects in the stack
skewed newsy slide-in for lower thirds
avoid: scaling a 1080p shot above ~130% (visible softness)
forgetting Use Composition’s Shutter Angle = 0 when you want its own blur
rotating or skewing without scaling up enough: black corners appear (125% scale with 8 degrees rotation and 10 skew still shows black wedges)

params.name: Position
params.typical: [960, 540] centre; offset 1920 px for a whip slide

params.name: Uniform Scale
params.does: Checkbox: 1 = one scale value, 0 = separate width/height

params.name: Scale Height
params.does: Vertical scale %; acts as the single Scale value when Uniform Scale = 1

params.name: Scale Width
params.does: Horizontal scale %, only used when Uniform Scale = 0

params.name: Rotation
params.typical: -5 to 5 for tilt or shake; 90-360 for spins

params.name: Use Composition’s Shutter Angle
params.does: 1 = use comp motion-blur settings, 0 = use the effect's own Shutter Angle

params.name: Shutter Angle
params.does: Motion blur amount for animated transform values (0-360)

cards.scripting: Scale and position are layer-space pixels. With Uniform Scale = 1 the visible 'Scale' control is the Scale Height property; set Scale Height, not Scale Width. The property name contains a curly apostrophe (U+2019): 'Use Composition’s Shutter Angle'. Motion blur only appears when a transform property is animated and Shutter Angle > 0 with that checkbox = 0. Order matters: effects below Transform see the transformed image. For the punch-in recipe set static Uniform Scale = 1, Use Composition’s Shutter Angle = 0 and Shutter Angle = 180 first.

verified.note: Image is scaled up, rotated about 8 degrees and skewed, with black wedges in the top-right and bottom-left corners where the tilted layer no longer covers the frame.

cards.name: Turbulent Displace
cards.summary: Displaces pixels with fractal noise so the image ripples, melts or wobbles organically, from subtle heat haze to heavy liquid warping.
use_for: heat-haze shimmer over a desert or rally ground shot
dream / memory flashback transition
liquid distortion transition between two shots in a trailer
wavy flag or banner on a still image
glitchy organic distortion on titles
avoid: high Amount on faces in serious news (looks grotesque)
setting Pinning to an unpinned option on full-frame footage (edges pull in transparency; keep the default or scale the layer up)
static Evolution on video makes it look frozen

params.name: Displacement
params.does: Type of noise displacement (turbulent, bulge, twist, smoother variants, horizontal/vertical/cross)

params.name: Evolution
params.typical: animate 0 -> 360 over 2-4 s, or expression time*90

params.name: Pinning
params.typical: 3 (default, believed to be Pin All) keeps the frame edges fixed on full-frame footage; other indices include separators, verify before use

cards.scripting: Displacement and Pinning popups include separator entries in their index range (max 11 / 17 for ~9 real choices), so only use indices you have verified; 1 = Turbulent is safe. Evolution is an angle in degrees. Offset is in layer pixels. Resize Layer = 1 lets displacement extend past layer bounds.

verified.note: Strong organic liquid warping across the whole frame (stripes, foreground blocks and figures melt and ripple) while the frame edges stay pinned.

cards.name: Twirl
cards.summary: Rotates the image around a centre point, twisting more at the centre than at the edge, producing a whirlpool swirl.
use_for: swirl transition: twist out of one shot, untwist into the next
dizzy / confused comic moment in a satire reel
hypnosis or propaganda-spin gag
swirl-in logo reveal
avoid: leaving a static twirl on a face (cheap 2000s look)

Twirl Radius above ~28 on 16:9 full-frame footage (radius is a percent of the width, so the swirl passes the top/bottom edges and pulls in black transparent wedges, very visible at 50); scale the layer up or precompose with padding
using it in serious documentary sections

params.name: Twirl Radius
params.does: Size of the twisted area as a percent of the layer
params.typical: 25-30 to stay inside a 16:9 frame; 50 reaches the left/right edges and pulls transparency in at top/bottom

cards.scripting: Angle is unbounded degrees. Twirl Radius is 0-100 percent of the larger layer dimension, not pixels; 50 makes the twirl reach the left/right edges of a 16:9 layer and pass the top/bottom edges, pulling transparent wedges into the swirl (verified in the gallery render). For a transition, keyframe the outgoing clip 0 -> 720 and the incoming clip -720 -> 0 around the cut.

verified.note: Whole frame is a strong whirlpool swirl; at Twirl Radius 50 on the 16:9 layer the swirl passes the top and bottom edges and pulls in large black transparent wedges.

cards.name: Warp
cards.summary: Bends the whole layer into one of Photoshop's warp-text shapes (arc, arch, bulge, flag, wave, fisheye, squeeze, twist and more).
use_for: arched or bulging headline text in reels and thumbnails
flag-wave on a logo or party symbol layer
squeeze / inflate comic emphasis on a word
retro poster type for trailer title cards
avoid: on full-frame live action (distorts the whole picture cheaply)
high Bend on small text (illegible)
warping text whose edges touch layer bounds (cropping)

params.name: Bend
params.does: Strength and direction of the warp

cards.scripting: Warp Style labels are read from After Effects 26.0 (15 entries; 14 is Twist and 15 Squeeze). Best applied to text or logo layers, or a precomp with padding so the warp is not clipped. Premiere has no direct equivalent; render it from AE (or build a MOGRT) or approximate with Wave Warp / Spherize.

verified.note: Bulge style stretches the middle of the frame vertically (upper detail pushed toward the top, centre detail pushed down) while the left and right edges stay closer to the original.

cards.name: Warp Stabilizer
cards.summary: Analyses shaky footage and smooths or locks the camera move, warping and cropping the frame to hide the correction. Corrective; on a still or locked-off shot there is nothing to stabilise.
use_for: smooth shaky handheld rally / ground-report footage
turn a handheld shot into a locked-off tripod look (No Motion)
steady phone footage in user-generated news clips
steady drone or vehicle B-roll before speed ramps
avoid: Smoothness too high on walking shots: jelly warping and big crop
time-stretched or time-remapped layers (precompose first; in Premiere the clip must also match the sequence frame size)
fast action or heavy occlusion: Subspace Warp wobbles; switch Method to Position, Scale, Rotation

params.name: Result
params.does: Smooth the motion or remove it entirely

params.name: Smoothness
params.does: How much of the original camera move is smoothed (%)

params.name: Method
params.typical: 4 (Subspace Warp) default; 2 (Position, Scale, Rotation) if it wobbles

params.name: Framing
params.does: How edges are handled (crop, auto-scale, synthesize)

params.name: Crop Less <-> Smooth More
params.does: Trade-off between crop and smoothness; only used by the cropping Framing modes

Objective.6: Apply Motion to Target Over Original

cards.scripting: Needs moving footage plus a background analysis that starts after the effect is applied; rendering before analysis finishes shows an 'Analyzing' banner or an unchanged frame (there is no documented ExtendScript call to wait for it, low confidence; check the banner before rendering). Verified 2026-10-04: an aerender of a freshly applied instance shows the 'Analyzing in background (step 1 of 2)' banner over an otherwise untouched frame, without even the Additional Scale; let the analysis finish inside AE and save the project before rendering. Time-stretched or time-remapped layers must be precomposed first (whether AE also requires layer size = comp size is unverified, low confidence; precomposing to comp size is the safe route). Objective (1-6) and Target Layer are for reverse-stabilisation / applying motion to another layer; Target Layer is a layer reference and cannot be set from a spec. Changing Method or Detailed Analysis re-triggers analysis.

verified.note: Frame is the untouched clip with AE's blue 'Analyzing in background (step 1 of 2)' banner across the middle and no 110% scale: aerender rendered before the background analysis ran, which no demo value can fix, so status is now needs_input (needs analysis completed and saved in the project, on shaky footage).

previous.why: aerender rendered before the background analysis ran: a harness limit, not an effect fault

cards.name: Wave Warp
cards.summary: Pushes the image into travelling waves (sine, square, triangle, noise, etc.) that animate on their own via Wave Speed, from gentle flag ripples to harsh glitch slicing.
use_for: flag ripple on a still flag or banner graphic
underwater / dream / drunk wobble on a shot
short glitch hit with Square waves on a cut
heat-wave shimmer on a title
retro VHS wobble on archive footage
avoid: large Wave Height on faces in serious content
edges revealing transparency: use Pinning or scale the layer up
forgetting it animates even without keyframes (set Wave Speed 0 for a static warp)

params.name: Wave Type
params.typical: 1 Sine for ripples, 2 Square for glitch, 9 Smooth Noise for organic

params.name: Wave Speed
params.does: Waves per second; animates without keyframes

params.name: Phase
params.does: Starting point of the wave cycle (degrees)
params.typical: 0; keyframe instead of speed for exact control

cards.scripting: Pinning has 11 indices but includes separator entries; 1 = None is safe, verify others before use. Direction and Phase are degrees. Wave Height/Width are pixels. Wave Speed drives motion over time, so the same frame differs at different times.

verified.note: Clear sine-wave ripples bend verticals and block edges across the frame, with scalloped black transparent edges along the top and bottom.

cards.name: 3D Point Control
cards.summary: Adds an [x, y, z] point value to a layer that expressions on other properties can read. Renders nothing by itself.
use_for: single control for a 3D camera target or light position in explainer scenes
master position for several 3D layers (map pins, floating cards)
template rig on a control null in a reusable trailer/explainer project
avoid: expecting any visible change without expressions
renaming the effect by script or building names into strings after expressions reference it (UI renames usually update simple references, scripted ones may not)

params.name: 3D Point
params.does: The [x, y, z] value read by expressions

cards.scripting: Value is a 3-element array [x, y, z] in pixels. Usually added to a null; read with thisComp.layer("Controls").effect("3D Point Control")("3D Point"). Name the effect instance before writing expressions. Mostly for 3D layers, cameras and lights; for 2D values use Point Control.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (expression control, renders nothing by itself), so no gallery frame was rendered.

cards.name: Angle Control
cards.summary: Adds an angle dial (degrees, with revolutions) to a layer for expressions to read. Renders nothing by itself.
use_for: one dial driving rotation of several layers (clock hands, map arrows, gears)
exposed angle control for a MOGRT / Essential Graphics template
driving Directional Blur or gradient direction from a single control
avoid: expecting a visible change without expressions
renaming the effect by script after expressions reference it (scripted renames may not update expression links)

params.name: Angle
params.does: Angle value in degrees read by expressions

cards.scripting: Value is degrees (unbounded; 360 = one revolution). Read with effect("Angle Control")("Angle"). Add to a control null, name it, then link expressions.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (expression control, renders nothing by itself), so no gallery frame was rendered.

cards.name: Checkbox Control
cards.summary: Adds an on/off checkbox (0 or 1) to a layer for expressions to read. Renders nothing by itself.
use_for: toggle a layer, logo or watermark on/off via an opacity expression
switch between two versions (Hindi / English text) in a template
exposed on/off option in a Premiere MOGRT via Essential Graphics
avoid: expecting a visible change without expressions
expecting smooth fades from it: checkbox keyframes are hold-only, use a Slider Control for fades
cards.scripting: Set as a number 0 or 1, not true/false. Typical expression on Opacity: effect("Checkbox Control")("Checkbox") == 1 ? 100 : 0. Add to a control null, name it, then link.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (expression control, renders nothing by itself), so no gallery frame was rendered.
